target: src/peditor（P3 新增與修改的程式）
focus_areas: Save transaction in the main process (export/transaction.py, service.destination_token/export_document, cli.py)
Worker-side export validation and write (worker/export.py text_check/visual_check/export_document, edit.apply_edit applied list)
Undo/redo command-log replay and apply rollback (worker/edit.py, analyzer reopen, server replay, service command log)

findings.title: Draft JSON gets no schema check: a malformed draft crashes list_drafts on every launch and leaves recover_draft half-done
findings.description: DraftStore.load only checks that the value is a dict and saved_at is a number. list() (80-82) indexes draft_id/path/sha256/position directly, so one draft missing a key raises KeyError and hides all valid drafts for up to 7 days. recover_draft (service.py:250-276) opens draft['path'] first, then uses log/position unchecked: max(e['base_revision'] ...) and log[:position] raise TypeError/KeyError/ValueError, and only ServiceError is caught, so the just-opened document stays open. A negative or too-large position passes replay and leaves an inconsistent doc.position (redo IndexError), which _save_draft then writes back.
findings.exploit_scenario: A corrupted or planted draft file in %LOCALAPPDATA%\PEditor\drafts makes every list_drafts() call raise, or leaves an orphaned open document when the user selects it.
findings.recommendation: Validate the schema in load() (draft_id == file stem, str path, 64-hex sha256, list of dicts with int base_revision >= 0 and dict params, int position in [0, len(log)], finite saved_at); treat failures as corrupt. In recover_draft, close the document on any exception.

findings.title: The 7-day expiry never triggers when saved_at is NaN, Infinity, or in the future
findings.description: _expired computes `not isinstance(saved,(int,float)) or now - saved > RETENTION_S`. json.loads accepts NaN/Infinity; NaN and +inf never compare as expired, and a future timestamp (clock skew) delays expiry by the skew. .tmp and unparsable files use st_mtime and have the same future-mtime weakness. Drafts contain the new plaintext, so this breaks the spec P3 retention rule and ADR-0020 §5.
findings.exploit_scenario: The clock was ahead when the draft was saved; after correction the draft with confidential text stays indefinitely. A planted saved_at: NaN makes a draft permanent.
findings.recommendation: Reject NaN/Infinity (parse_constant), require math.isfinite, and treat saved_at in the future as expired/corrupt.

findings.title: list() reports the draft_id written inside the file, not the filename, so discard or recover can act on a different draft
findings.description: list() loads each file by its filename stem but returns data['draft_id'] from the contents without checking it matches. recover_draft and discard_draft then act on folder/<id>.json. A mismatch makes discard delete another draft (or nothing) while the listed draft stays, and recover open a different draft than the one shown.
findings.exploit_scenario: A corrupted A.json with draft_id B: the user discards the entry for A, B.json is deleted and A.json with its plaintext stays.
findings.recommendation: Return the filename stem as draft_id, or reject files whose draft_id differs from the stem.

findings.title: recover_draft opens the raw path stored in the draft file before any validation
findings.description: draft['path'] from the JSON file goes straight to open_document and the worker; type, absoluteness and UNC/device paths are not checked, and the SHA-256 comparison happens only after the worker has opened the file. On Windows a UNC path makes the worker contact an SMB host (breaking offline guarantee, leaking NTLM). Requires same-user write access to the drafts folder and the user choosing the draft.
findings.exploit_scenario: A planted draft with path \\attacker\s\report.pdf; when selected the worker connects over SMB before the hash mismatch rejects it.
findings.recommendation: Require path to be a str absolute local path; reject UNC, \\?\ and \\.\ paths; require an existing regular file.

findings.title: Main process takes revision numbers and plan ids from the worker without checking them, and updates the log before reading new_revision
findings.description: apply_edit/undo/redo set doc.revision = result['new_revision'] without checking it is doc.revision + 1; plan_text_edit stores plan_id and preconditions.revision from the worker. apply_edit truncates/appends the log and increments position before reading new_revision; a missing key leaves log advanced but revision not. When the plan entry is missing the main process raises while the worker is already at R+1. A compromised worker can return a stale new_revision so that after restart the restore uses an old revision number and caller-held target_ids/expected_revision match again.
findings.exploit_scenario: A compromised worker returns new_revision equal to an earlier revision, then crashes; after restore old target_ids pass revision checks against different content.
findings.recommendation: Compute the next revision in the main process and require the worker value to match; validate plan ids and preconditions; read results before mutating the log; restart the worker on desync.

findings.title: Command log keeps a reference to the caller's editable_region list
findings.description: plan_text_edit stores the caller's editable_region list object in params and logs that same dict. A later mutation by the caller silently changes what undo/redo/restore/drafts replay, including allowed_change_mask used by the export visual check.
findings.exploit_scenario: UI reuses its selection-rectangle list; after an undo or worker crash the replayed edit uses an enlarged region, widening the area ignored by the visual check.

findings.title: apply_edit, undo and redo report failure after the edit is committed when saving the draft fails
findings.description: _advance updates revision and clears plans, then _save_draft calls DraftStore.save which re-raises OSError. The worker has committed and the log/position are updated, but the caller receives an exception (not even a ServiceError).
findings.exploit_scenario: Drafts folder full or locked: the user sees an error, assumes the edit was not applied, and saves a file that contains it.
findings.recommendation: Make draft persistence best-effort (catch OSError, report as warning) or save the draft before committing in-memory state.

findings.title: Undo and worker-restart restore replay the whole log in one request with a fixed 30 s timeout, so edits can become unsaveable
findings.description: undo sends log[:position-1] and the restart restore sends log[:position] as single replay requests under REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S=30. Each replayed command does a full reopen (edit.py:410 only to set the revision), _references walk, pike.save and reopen; cost is driven by the PDF. If the sum exceeds 30 s, undo times out, the worker restarts, and every later _doc_call (including export) repeats the failing restore; the except path's close_document on the new worker masks the original error.
findings.exploit_scenario: A large or object-heavy PDF makes each edit take 3-5 s; after about 10 edits undo times out and the document can no longer be saved.
findings.recommendation: Replay in chunks or scale the timeout with command count; drop the redundant reopen; consider log+snapshot; do not mask the original error.

findings.title: No-overwrite rule is enforced only by an earlier check; os.replace always clobbers the destination
findings.description: destination() rejects an existing file when overwrite=False and records state None; _check re-reads file_state before os.replace, which replaces unconditionally. A file created at the destination between the last check and os.replace is overwritten, contrary to ADR-0020 §3.4.
findings.exploit_scenario: A sync client writes a colleague's report.pdf into the folder right before the rename; it is overwritten without a conflict error.
findings.recommendation: When state is None, use a non-clobbering rename (os.link+unlink on POSIX, os.rename on Windows).

findings.title: Raw OSError with the full path escapes the save transaction; fsync failure after replace reported as failure
findings.description: file_state calls sha256_file without catching open errors (locked/unreadable destination); sha256_file(temp) raises FileNotFoundError if the worker reports success without a file; _fsync_dir can fail after os.replace succeeded. destination_token/export_document only translate ProtocolError and the CLI only catches ServiceError, so the OSError (with the full path) reaches the caller/stderr, and in the fsync case a completed save is reported as failed with the token not consumed.
findings.exploit_scenario: Exporting over a PDF locked by a viewer crashes with PermissionError containing the full path in stderr.
findings.recommendation: Convert OSError to ProtocolError without paths; treat post-replace fsync failure as success with a warning and always consume the token.

findings.title: A temp file with the full document can stay in the user's folder indefinitely when cleanup fails
findings.description: _remove ignores every OSError; stale temps are only removed by a later commit into the same folder after 600 s. A worker still holding the handle after kill timeout, antivirus/indexer locks, or a main-process crash leave .~peditor-*.tmp.pdf next to the destination until the user saves into that folder again.
findings.exploit_scenario: A timed-out save in a synced folder leaves a full copy of the edited document that is synced to the cloud.
findings.recommendation: Retry deletion, record failed temp paths in app state and clean at startup/exit, report a warning.

findings.title: Overwrite by rename replaces the destination's mode/ACL with the temp file's defaults
findings.description: The worker creates the temp with default permissions; os.replace swaps the directory entry, so an overwritten destination loses a restrictive mode (e.g. 0600), explicit ACL or ownership.
findings.exploit_scenario: A 0600 confidential.pdf in a group-readable directory becomes 0644 after an overwrite save.
findings.recommendation: Copy the existing destination's mode to the temp before replace (best-effort ACL), or create temps 0600.

findings.title: Visual-check mask defaults to glyph boxes that an embedded font can inflate
findings.description: Without editable_region, allowed_change_mask is the union of MuPDF char bboxes (_selection_box), derived from font ascender/descender which an embedded font controls; nothing bounds it. visual_check ignores all pixels inside it, so a crafted font can draw changes far from the baseline inside the inflated band. VISUAL_OUTSIDE_LIMIT is also a fraction of pixels, so at reduced zoom up to ~5000 pixels may change outside the mask.
findings.exploit_scenario: A font with +/-20000 unit metrics makes the replacement glyph also draw a minus sign 200 pt below; the default mask covers it and the save passes.
findings.recommendation: Derive the default mask from computed baseline geometry and font size; clamp masks to the crop box; use an absolute pixel limit.

findings.title: text_check is a whole-page substring test, so text already elsewhere on the page satisfies it
findings.description: text_check tests whether the whitespace-stripped new text occurs anywhere in the whitespace-stripped page text, not within the edited region and not compared to the original. An existing (possibly invisible) copy satisfies it. The overlap skip drops an edit whenever a later edit's mask overlaps, and masks can be inflated (F-013).
findings.exploit_scenario: A page already contains hidden '1,000,000'; the user changes a visible amount to '1,000,000' with codes that extract incorrectly, and text_check still passes.
findings.recommendation: Extract text clipped to the edit mask (page.get_text(clip=...)), or compare occurrence counts with the original; only skip when a later mask contains the earlier one.

findings.title: Pure-Python pixel loop over up to 50 MP per edited page lets a crafted PDF make Save exceed the 30 s timeout
findings.description: visual_check renders two pixmaps of up to MAX_RENDER_PIXELS (50 MP) and _outside_pixels iterates every pixel of every differing row in Python, with a generator per pixel for mask spans. A huge page with very large text makes a one-character edit change thousands of full-width rows, giving 10^7-5*10^7 Python iterations per page; the request exceeds 30 s and the document can never be saved.
findings.exploit_scenario: One 3500x3500 pt page with 2000 pt text; changing '100' to '200' makes every save time out.
findings.recommendation: Zero mask spans by slicing and compare rows as bytes, or use pixmap operations; cap the visual-check pixel budget below MAX_RENDER_PIXELS and return RESOURCE_LIMIT.
